title: On Hiding the money under the floor
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：hide　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 hide 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1982 the fisherman ① hid the money under the floor before dawn, and every boatman in the harbour said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three seasons on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the fisherman ② hides the money under the floor in public without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ hide the money under the floor at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ hidden the money under the floor before — a line in the logbook for July 1976 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Hiding the money under the floor before dawn, the fisherman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the net at the far pier, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ hide the view from the window in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Hide the view from the window at once and never mention it again.

By 1989 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the logbook, and a new boatman from the next harbour ⑧ hides the view from the window before dawn every season without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the pier, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ hid the money under the floor again when nobody else would.

⑩ To hide the money under the floor, my mother said in 1994, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the harbour remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the harbour forgets, somebody hides the money under the floor in public again and somebody must hide the money under the floor before dawn all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 藏（一般过去式 hid the money under the floor：1982 年渔人头一回这样做，天没亮就）
B. v. 藏（一般现在 hides the money under the floor：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 藏（不定式 to hide the money under the floor：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 藏（过去完成时 had hidden the money under the floor：1976 年七月的航海日志上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 藏（动名词 hiding the money under the floor 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 遮住（hide the view from the window：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去遮住把窗外的景致遮住）
G. v. 遮住（hide the view from the window：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 藏（后段两处：新来的船工照例 hides the view from the window，而母亲又一次 hid the money under the floor）

answers.why: hide 意为“藏”，1982 年渔人天没亮就藏把钱藏在地板下面，那是渔港里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 hid。
hide 意为“藏”，自那以后渔人当着众人面把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 hides。
hide 意为“藏”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯藏把钱藏在地板下面”，此处为不定式 to hide the money under the floor。
hide 意为“藏”，航海日志里 七月 那行字说明早在 1989 年之前就有人藏过，故用过去完成时 had hidden。
hide 意为“藏”，渔人说“藏把钱藏在地板下面这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 hiding the money under the floor 作主语。
hide 意为“遮住”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去遮住把窗外的景致遮住”，should ever 之后用原形 hide the view from the window。
hide 意为“遮住”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻遮住把窗外的景致遮住（hide the view from the window at once），以后再也不要提起。
hide 意为“藏”，新来的船工每个汛期都照例遮住把窗外的景致遮住，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 hides。
hide 意为“藏”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次天没亮就藏把钱藏在地板下面，用一般过去式 hid 叙述。
hide 意为“藏”，结尾那句是母亲 1994 年的话：要藏把钱藏在地板下面，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和渔港记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 hide 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1982 the fisherman hid the money under the floor before dawn, and nobody in the harbour forgot it.
Even now the fisherman hides the money under the floor in public whenever the harbour asks.
Hiding the money under the floor before dawn, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever hide the view from the window in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new boatman from the next harbour hides the view from the window before dawn every season, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother hid the money under the floor again, and the harbour remembered that half.
